investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: plain curl GET (descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser) of the candidate official domain and several known static paths. The first domain found by search (loophole-berlin.com) turned out on direct inspection to be an unrelated parked/for-sale domain, not the venue's own site — WebSearch is a discovery lead only and was NOT trusted as authority; the real official domain (loophole.berlin) was found via a second, more specific search and confirmed as the venue's own (its 500-error page names the contact 'webmaster@loophole-berlin.atelierkbg.com', tying the domain to the venue's own hosting). Every path attempted on the real domain (homepage, /press-statement/, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml) returned a genuine server-side error (403/500), not a rendered page — no event data was retrievable.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the venue's real official domain (https://loophole.berlin/) returned HTTP 403 'Forbidden' (Apache generic error page, not a rendered page) for the homepage, and HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error' for /press-statement/, /robots.txt, and /sitemap.xml — every path attempted returned a genuine server-side error, never actual page content. This is consistent with independent discovery-lead context found via WebSearch (not treated as source authority) that the venue was banned from hosting concerts by the Ordnungsamt Berlin in July 2024 and has been seeking a new location — the official site appears genuinely broken/unmaintained, not merely bot-blocked. No event data, JSON-LD, feed, or API could be inspected because no page actually rendered.

identity.notes: The domain loophole.berlin is very likely the venue's genuine official domain — its own 500-error page names a hosting contact 'webmaster@loophole-berlin.atelierkbg.com', directly tying the domain to the venue's name — but this could not be independently corroborated against the venue's own rendered content, because every page on the domain returned a server error (403/500) rather than actual content. identity.status is honestly recorded as AMBIGUOUS rather than PROVEN: strong circumstantial evidence (the error-page contact address), but no genuinely rendered first-party page content was ever retrieved to confirm it directly. A DIFFERENT domain, loophole-berlin.com, was initially surfaced by search and is explicitly NOT this venue — it is a parked/for-sale domain (its own retained page states 'This domain may be for sale!') and was rejected as a candidate rather than trusted.

blockers.description: The venue's official domain (loophole.berlin) returns a genuine server-side error (403/500) on every path attempted — homepage, press-statement page, robots.txt, and sitemap.xml. No content, event data, or platform fingerprint of any kind could be retrieved. Combined with the independently-found context that the venue was banned from hosting concerts in July 2024 and is seeking relocation, this reads as a genuinely broken/inactive site rather than a temporary glitch.

reasons: The venue's real official domain is identifiable with reasonable confidence (loophole.berlin, corroborated by its own error-page hosting contact) but returns only server errors (403/500) on every path tried — no event data, platform fingerprint, or even a rendered homepage could be retrieved.
A first, search-surfaced candidate domain (loophole-berlin.com) was correctly identified and rejected as an unrelated parked/for-sale domain rather than assumed to be the venue.

Independent discovery-lead context (not treated as source authority) indicates the physical venue was banned from hosting concerts by the Ordnungsamt Berlin in July 2024 and has been seeking a new location — consistent with a genuinely inactive/broken official site, not a transient error.

Per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md, DEFER is a legitimate, complete investigation outcome when reliable, honest automated acquisition cannot be established safely — escalating to a Level 2 structural probe would have nothing to inspect (every response is a bare server-generated error page with no application content, JS, or bootstrap data of any kind), so no genuine escalation opportunity exists to attempt.
This investigation should be revisited later (a new investigation_id, superseding this one) if/when the venue relaunches at a new location with a working site.
